feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-x{y}^{′}+6y=0,\,x>0.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Note that the given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}-x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+6{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }-\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+6{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-\lambda +6] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-\lambda +6 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +6 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We solve the auxiliary equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +1 & =-5 \\ (\lambda -1)^{2} & =-5 \\ \lambda -1 & =\pm \sqrt{5}\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =1\pm \sqrt{5}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the roots are $\lambda =1\pm \sqrt{5}\text{i}.$

Now, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{1+\sqrt{5}\text{i}} & =x{e}^{\text{i}\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}=x(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)), \\ {x}^{1-\sqrt{5}\text{i}} & =x{e}^{-\text{i}\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}=x(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & =A{x}^{1+\sqrt{5}\text{i}}+B{x}^{1-\sqrt{5}\text{i}} \\  & =Ax(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x))+Bx(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)) \\  & =(A+B)x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\text{i}(A-B)x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite $y(x)$ as 

$$
y(x)=x({c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)),
$$

where ${c}_{1}=A+B$ and ${c}_{2}=\text{i}(A-B).$
